claims.claim: Milky seas are rare expanses of steady whitish marine bioluminescence visible at night.
Luminous bacteria are implicated, but their precise ecological relationships and conditions producing milky seas remain uncertain.
At high bacterial population density, chemical quorum sensing can trigger bacterial luminescence.
A 1985 sampled milky sea contained luminous bacteria associated with microalgae.
The glow may persist for days to weeks and drift with surface currents.
The VIIRS day-night band can detect the faint glow from orbit under favorable conditions; moonlight and clouds can complicate detection.
Unlike a milky sea’s steady glow, mechanically stimulated dinoflagellate bioluminescence typically flashes briefly.
